newsitem.title: SWEDEN: SWIMMING-CHEN WINS WOMEN'S 200 BACKSTROKE WORLD TITLE.
newsitem.headline: SWIMMING-CHEN WINS WOMEN'S 200 BACKSTROKE WORLD TITLE.

text.p: Chen Yan won China's fifth title on the final day of the world short-course swimming championships and denied American Misty Hyman gold at the last gasp on Sunday.
Hyman led through the first 150 metres but Chen steadily cut back the lead and just edged out the American on the final stroke to win in two minutes 07.50 seconds.
Hyman, bronze medallist in the 100 backstroke and 100 and 200 butterfly, took the silver in 2:07.66.

It was tough for the American, who won the 100 backstroke gold at the 1995 edition of these championships, but she turned to embrace team mate Lea Oberstar after she saw from the electronic scoreboard that they had both gained medals.
Oberstar overhauled Germany's Antje Buschschulte to take the bronze in 2:08.29.
Germany's Sabine Herbst finished fifth, back in the water with little respite after finishing fourth in the 200 individual medley two events earlier.
